unlisted_practices: Journals should add a peer-reviewed structured interpretive metadata layer (SIMcard) to published biomedical articles in machine-readable format such as XML or JSON so AI systems can access verified interpretive boundaries.

Journals should publish a plain-language FACTS label with each article stating the primary claim, causal or associational status, context and generalizability, limitations, prohibited inferences, and recommended interpretation.

AI developers should design retrieval-augmented generation and agentic systems to preferentially query and reason over structured interpretive metadata, and incorporate such metadata into pretraining and fine-tuning.
Journals, indexing services, and AI developers should coordinate to align on interpretive metadata standards.
Authors, reviewers and editors, and publishers should share responsibility for interpretive framing, with SIMcard and FACTS labels reviewable and amendable when errors are identified.
Researchers should empirically evaluate whether interpretive metadata improves AI interpretive fidelity using adversarial prompting with and without metadata.

screen.reason: Commentary/viewpoint discussing guardrails and recommendations for scientific communication and AI interpretation of biomedical research.
